content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate milk drink is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from whole milk, cocoa mass, sugar, and sometimes added flavorings such as vanilla or sea salt. It has a sweet, creamy taste with a pronounced chocolate note and is usually served cold or slightly warmed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial chocolate milk drink appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Cocoa content typically ranges from 2 % to 5 % of the total volume.
In some countries the drink is sold as a concentrate that is reconstituted with water or milk.
Chocolate milk is often used as a base for desserts, smoothies, and sauces.
In Russia its popularity grew after brands introduced organic milk and "clean" cocoa versions.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Milk, the main ingredient, provides calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The drink contains riboflavin (B2) and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa mass is high in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Theobromine and small amounts of caffeine in cocoa can boost alertness and improve mood.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: The water content of milk contributes to overall fluid balance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People lacking lactase may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consumption.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may have an allergic reaction to cocoa components.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A 250 ml serving contains roughly 150–200 kcal, which should be considered in a calorie‑controlled diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate milk drink can be enjoyed straight from the carton, added to coffee, blended into smoothies, or used as a base for milkshakes. If desired, gently warm it in the microwave, but avoid boiling to preserve flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the drink refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as thawing may alter the texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Creamed egg is a boiled egg whose yolk is replaced with a smooth cream made from milk, cream, and sugar. The dish originated in the 1950s and quickly became a popular dessert in Soviet canteens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Creamed egg was often served at festive menus for New Year and Victory Day.
The cream was made only with whole milk and sugar, without egg yolks.
Original recipes sweetened the cream with honey and sometimes added vanilla sugar.
The dish got the name “egg‑cream” because of its visual similarity to a boiled egg.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Creamed egg provides protein from the egg white, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: The milk‑based cream supplies calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The dish is calorie‑rich, which can be beneficial during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to egg whites may experience reactions up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The creamy layer contains a considerable amount of sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Cream adds saturated fats, which should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve creamed egg chilled, often garnished with berries or dusted with powdered sugar. It can be eaten as a standalone dessert or used as a filling for cakes and pastries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep creamed egg refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap, and consume within 2–3 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

content.title: About
content.content: Grilled salmon retains a tender, smoky flavor while offering a rich nutritional profile. It is a popular choice for healthy eating because the fish provides high‑quality protein, beneficial fatty acids, and a variety of vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon is one of the few fish that contains significant amounts of the omega‑3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.
Wild salmon generally contains more nutrients than farm‑raised salmon.
Grilling helps preserve a large portion of vitamin D, which is important for bones and immunity.
Salmon can change the color of its flesh depending on its diet; those that eat krill have a brighter orange hue.
In Japan, grilled salmon is often served with soy sauce and lemon to highlight its natural taste.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health, lower triglyceride levels, and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Salmon protein is easily digestible and essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Salmon is one of the best dietary sources of vitamin D, crucial for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and participates in red blood cell formation.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Some salmon may contain traces of mercury or polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs); moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Certain individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Excessive grilling can create harmful compounds such as acrylamide, so cook salmon until golden but not dry.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled salmon hot, sliced into portions. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, olive oil, or soy sauce. Great alongside vegetable sides, quinoa, mashed potatoes, or fresh salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh salmon fillets in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in film or an airtight container, for up to 2 days. Frozen salmon retains quality for up to 3 months at –18 °C. Thaw in the fridge before cooking and pat dry.
